approved_for_manuscript_by_agent_review.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational.
Create an austere publication-ready scientific FLOW DIAGRAM on white, landscape 2.6:1, for a computer science paper. This is a second architecture illustration. Use small plain rectangular nodes, crisp straight black arrows, thin black strokes, square corners, Times-like serif labels. Only one muted blue stroke to emphasize the last row. No decorative title, no colors filling backgrounds, gradients, shadows, icons, silhouettes, dancers, cartoons, rounded cards, artwork, decorative music, or data plots. It should look like a precise vector diagram drafted by an academic researcher, not a generated infographic.
Purpose: compare FOUR implemented CONTROL POLICIES over the SAME music-to-text choreography task, not their measured performance. Use four aligned horizontal lanes with identical input/output positions. An unobtrusive top brace over all rows says "Same windows, candidates, style, acoustic evidence, outer LLM, and budget caps". Make arrows simple and unambiguous and all labels large enough to read at full paper width.
Row 1 label "Workflow". Rectangular nodes in exact order: "Outline" → "Compose unit" → "Validate" → "Commit". Small routed arrow from Commit back to Compose unit labeled "next unit".
Row 2 label "Self-Refine adaptation". Nodes: "Outline" → "Draft" → "Self-feedback" → "Revise" → "Validate + commit". Small return arrow from final node to Draft labeled "next unit". Do not add unlimited revision loops.
Row 3 label "ReAct adaptation". Nodes: "Outline" → "Choose tool" → "Execute" → "Observe". A routed return arrow from Observe to Choose tool labeled "bounded tool loop"; a separate arrow out of Execute to a small terminal node "Commit unit". Use no tool icons.
Row 4 label "Proposed harness". Nodes: "Music / motif objectives" → "Compose with history" → "Validate + commit" → "Targeted repeat revision". A return arrow from Validate + commit to Compose with history labeled "next unit"; the arrow to Targeted repeat revision is labeled "after all units". Put a very small note below this last node "remaining budget only".
Below all rows a single shared thin outlined strip labeled "Harness contract: persistent state · time bounds · protected regions · call/token accounting · logged failures".
Important: this figure shows control flow, not reward learning, not physical motion generation, not numerical results, not a claim of superiority. Avoid labels such as best, optimal, state of the art, quality gain. Keep all four rows equally readable and no performance values. These names are task adaptations of published methods. Exact concise wording and careful feedback routing.
